title: Is Instinct safe to use? Three things to know before you sign up

reading.body:
Instinct is an AI personal assistant that collects user data for model training by default, with no explicit prior authorization required. Users must actively opt out or use a protected feature to prevent sensitive information like browsing habits, location, and financial data from being used this way. The system also retains indexed copies of data from connected accounts indefinitely even after disconnection, unless users specifically request deletion. These practices represent a deployment choice to prioritize convenience and data collection over default privacy protection.

The assistant can execute purchases on users' behalf, but the system was deployed without placing Instinct between the user and merchant in case of disputes. This means problems fall outside Instinct's responsibility. What would have caught these issues is a privacy-first architecture where data collection and retention required explicit consent, where disconnection meant deletion, and where financial transactions required real-time user approval rather than standing authority.

It is not established whether these are design flaws, negligence, or intentional trade-offs, or what recourse users have if they discover unauthorized use of their data.

summary:
# Summary

Instinct is an AI personal assistant that offers convenience but raises significant privacy and security concerns. According to a Norton security analysis, users should be aware of three major risks before signing up. First, Instinct may use personal information to train its AI models by default, unless users actively opt out or use the protected Vault feature, meaning sensitive data like browsing habits, location, and financial information could be used without direct authorization. Second, even when users disconnect connected accounts like Gmail, Instinct may retain copies of indexed data indefinitely unless deletion is specifically requested. Third, the assistant can make purchases on users' behalf, and if problems arise, disputes fall between the user and merchant rather than with Instinct.

Norton emphasizes that users should not have to sacrifice privacy for AI assistance. The company positions its Norton Family Assistant as an alternative that prioritizes data protection, stating that information shared is not used to train external AI models and that users must explicitly approve actions like form submissions before they occur. Users can easily delete data by removing their Norton account or through the assistant settings.
